```bash copy
(curl -fsSL --retry 4 --retry-delay 3 https://dl.andronix.app/get.sh -o $PREFIX/tmp/get.sh || curl -4 -fsSL --retry 2 --retry-delay 3 https://dl.andronix.app/get.sh -o $PREFIX/tmp/get.sh) && sh $PREFIX/tmp/get.sh install debian --de xfce
```

Replace `debian` and `xfce` with your distro and desktop. See [Installing without the app](/termux/without-the-app).

results.title: The andronix Command
results.text:

```bash
# install Debian 13 with the XFCE desktop
andronix install debian --de xfce

# open Debian (same as ./start-debian.sh)
andronix start debian

# open Debian's desktop full screen in Termux:X11
andronix desktop debian

# what's installed, and what you can install
andronix list

# update andronix and every installed distro

# save Debian to your phone's storage
andronix backup debian --to storage

# pick a backup and bring it back
andronix restore

# make the desktop lighter
andronix tune debian --profile light

# add a dev pack (python, node, java, go, db)
andronix pack add debian python

# delete Debian

# delete a Modded OS edition, by its edition id (installer 2.0.1+)

# show the version, e.g. andronix 2.0.0
andronix version

# show help
```

output.title: The andronix Command
output.text:
In Andronix 2.0, every free distro is installed and managed by one command, `andronix`. The install command the app copies for you sets it up in Termux, so you don't need to install anything by hand. This page lists everything `andronix` can do.

**This command is for Andronix with Termux**: older phones (Android 7, or no 64-bit ARM processor) and the command-line installer. For distros in the app, use the app's buttons; inside such a distro, only `sudo andronix pack` works (see [Dev packs](/use/dev-packs)).

You'll usually never type most of these. The app copies the right install command, and `./start-.sh` still starts your distro. This page is for when you want more control.

## Quick reference

Run these in **Termux** (not inside the distro):

```bash
# install Debian 13 with the XFCE desktop
andronix install debian --de xfce

# open Debian (same as ./start-debian.sh)
andronix start debian

# open Debian's desktop full screen in Termux:X11
andronix desktop debian

# what's installed, and what you can install
andronix list

# update andronix and every installed distro
andronix update

# save Debian to your phone's storage
andronix backup debian --to storage

# pick a backup and bring it back
andronix restore

# make the desktop lighter
andronix tune debian --profile light

# add a dev pack (python, node, java, go, db)
andronix pack add debian python

# delete Debian
andronix remove debian

# delete a Modded OS edition, by its edition id (installer 2.0.1+)
andronix remove ubuntu-kde

# free the space of leftover downloads (installer 2.0.1+)
andronix clean

# check this phone and what Andronix adjusts for it (installer 2.0.1+)
andronix doctor

# report a failed command to Andronix; shows everything first (installer 2.0.2+)
andronix report

# show the version, e.g. andronix 2.0.0
andronix version

# show help
andronix help
```

Run these **inside the distro**:

```bash
# start the desktop
vncserver-start

# stop the desktop
vncserver-stop
```

## Getting andronix

The Andronix app (10.0 or newer) sets up `andronix` for you with its install command. Without the app, this one line downloads `andronix`, checks it, and runs an install:

```bash copy
(curl -fsSL --retry 4 --retry-delay 3 https://dl.andronix.app/get.sh -o $PREFIX/tmp/get.sh || curl -4 -fsSL --retry 2 --retry-delay 3 https://dl.andronix.app/get.sh -o $PREFIX/tmp/get.sh) && sh $PREFIX/tmp/get.sh install debian --de xfce
```

Replace `debian` and `xfce` with the distro and desktop you want. After that, `andronix` is installed in Termux and you can use it directly. If Termux doesn't have `proot` yet, the installer installs it first. See [Install without the app](/termux/without-the-app).

`andronix update` keeps it up to date.

## Distro names

Use these names with `andronix install`, `start`, `remove` and `backup`.

| Name | Distro | CPU types | Start script |
|---|---|---|---|
| `debian` | Debian 13 | arm64, arm, x86, x86_64 | `./start-debian.sh` |
| `ubuntu` | Ubuntu 26.04 LTS | arm64, arm, x86_64 | `./start-ubuntu26.sh` or `./start-ubuntu22.sh` |
| `ubuntu24` | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS | arm64, arm, x86_64 | `./start-ubuntu.sh` or `./start-ubuntu20.sh` |
| `kali` | Kali Linux (rolling) | arm64, arm, x86, x86_64 | `./start-kali.sh` |
| `fedora` | Fedora 44 | arm64, x86_64 | `./start-fedora.sh` |
| `arch` | Arch Linux (Arch Linux ARM on phones) | arm64, arm, x86_64 | `./start-arch.sh` |
| `manjaro` | Manjaro ARM | arm64, x86_64 | `./start-manjaro.sh` |
| `alpine` | Alpine 3.24 | arm64, arm, x86, x86_64 | `./start-alpine.sh` |
| `void` | Void Linux (rolling) | arm64, arm, x86, x86_64 | `./start-void.sh` |

Most phones are **arm64**. Not sure what yours is? `andronix install` checks it for you and tells you if a distro doesn't support it.

## Modded OS edition ids

installer 2.0.1+

A [Modded OS](/modded-os/modded-os) edition is installed into the folder of the distro it's built on, and has its own id. You install it from the app (see [Installing Modded OS](/modded-os/modded-os-installation)); after that, `start`, `desktop`, `update`, `backup`, `doctor`, `tune`, `pack` and `remove` accept its id as well as the distro name.

| Edition id | Edition | Built on |
|---|---|---|
| `ubuntu-xfce` | Modded 2.0 Ubuntu XFCE | `ubuntu` |
| `ubuntu-kde` | Modded 2.0 Ubuntu KDE | `ubuntu` |
| `debian-xfce` | Modded 2.0 Debian XFCE | `debian` |
| `kali-xfce` | Modded 2.0 Kali XFCE | `kali` |
| `manjaro-xfce` | Modded 2.0 Manjaro XFCE | `manjaro` |
| `legacy-ubuntu-xfce` | Classic Ubuntu XFCE | `ubuntu` |
| `legacy-ubuntu-kde` | Classic Ubuntu KDE | `ubuntu` |
| `legacy-debian` | Classic Debian | `debian` |
| `legacy-manjaro` | Classic Manjaro | `manjaro` |

An edition id only works when that exact edition is the one installed. If the distro's folder holds something else (the free distro, or another edition), the command says what's installed there and which name to use instead.

**One install per distro.** A distro and the Modded editions built on it share one folder, so only one of them can be installed at a time. For example, the free Ubuntu, Modded 2.0 Ubuntu KDE and Classic Ubuntu XFCE can't be installed side by side. Installing a different one over it stops with a message; add `--reinstall` to replace it. It asks before deleting anything, so [back up](#backing-up-and-restoring) first if you want to keep your files.

## Installing

```bash
andronix install <distro> [--de <desktop>] [options]
```

`--de` picks the desktop. See [Desktop Environments](/reference/desktops) for help choosing.

| Desktop | What you get |
|---|---|
| `--de xfce` | XFCE, our recommended desktop |
| `--de lxqt` | LXQt, a light Qt desktop |
| `--de mate` | MATE, a classic desktop |
| `--de kde` | KDE Plasma, the most complete desktop. Debian, Ubuntu 26.04 and Kali only; needs 4 GB of RAM or more. |
| `--de none` | Command line only, no desktop |

`--de kde` on another distro stops with a message naming the distros that offer it. For old app buttons and commands, `--de lxde` installs LXQt, and the retired window managers (`i3`, `awesome`, `openbox`) and Enlightenment install XFCE, each with a notice.

Other options:

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--no-browser` | Don't install Firefox. Desktop installs include it by default. |
| `--no-start` | Don't open the distro when the install finishes. |
| `--reinstall` | Delete the distro and install it again from scratch. Also replaces a different edition installed in the same folder (see [Modded OS edition ids](#modded-os-edition-ids)). Asks before deleting. |
| `--yes` | Answer yes to every question. |
| `--plain` | No colours or animation, one line per step. Handy for logs. |

The installer shows each step with a ✓ as it finishes:

```text
✓ Installing proot          (only if Termux doesn't have it yet)
✓ Checking your phone
✓ Finding the best download
✓ Downloading Debian 13
✓ Unpacking files
✓ Setting up Debian 13
✓ Refreshing package lists
✓ Updating Debian 13
✓ Installing XFCE desktop · 250 packages
✓ Installing Firefox
✓ Setting up the desktop
✓ Writing start-debian.sh
```

Then it asks you to create your user (see [First login](#first-login)) and takes you into the distro.

If an install stops halfway (you closed Termux, lost the connection, or Android stopped it), run the **same command again**. It picks up where it left off.

## Where the files come from

The installer downloads a ready-made image of the distro from Andronix's servers. If that download isn't available, it falls back to the distro's official image (for example, from Docker Hub). Every download is checked before it's unpacked.

## First login

Free distros no longer log you in as `root`. The first time you start a distro, it asks you for:

1. **A username**, in lower-case letters and numbers, for example `alex`.
2. **A password** for that user. You'll need it for `sudo`.
3. **A desktop (VNC) password**, 6 to 8 characters. You can reuse your user password if it's 6 to 8 characters long. Desktop installs only.

After that, the distro always logs you in as that user, and your prompt looks like `alex@localhost`. Use `sudo` for anything that needs root, for example `sudo apt install nano`.

**Manjaro:** `sudo` doesn't work on Manjaro ARM in Andronix yet. For admin tasks, open a root shell from Termux with `andronix start manjaro --root`.

Forgot your password? In Termux, run `andronix start  --root` to get a root shell, then `passwd ` to set a new one.

## Starting a distro

```bash
andronix start <distro> [--root] [-- command...]
```

- `andronix start debian` opens a shell as your user. `./start-debian.sh` does exactly the same.
- `--root` opens a root shell instead.
- `--x11` opens the distro's desktop in Termux:X11 instead of a shell (same as `andronix desktop debian`).
- Anything after `--` runs inside the distro and then returns to Termux, for example `andronix start debian -- uname -a`. The old form `./start-debian.sh uname -a` works too.

Type `exit` to leave the distro and go back to Termux.

Each interactive start also makes sure Termux's PulseAudio is running, so [sound](/use/sound) works. One-off commands (after `--`) never install anything.

## Opening the desktop on Termux:X11

```bash
andronix desktop [<distro>]
andronix desktop stop
```

- Opens the distro's desktop full screen in the Termux:X11 app, as your user. With only one desktop install, the distro name is optional.
- Installs Termux's `termux-x11` package the first time. The Termux:X11 app itself comes from its GitHub release page; if it's missing, the command shows the link.
- `andronix desktop stop` (from another Termux session) stops it.

See [Termux:X11](/termux/termux-x11).

## Listing distros

```bash
andronix list
```

Shows what's installed (with its desktop and start script), any distros from the pre-2.0 installer, and every distro and desktop you can install.

## Updating

```bash
andronix update [<distro>]
```

Updates `andronix` itself, then the packages in every installed distro (or only the one you name). `--self` updates only `andronix`; `--no-self` only the distros. See [Keep it updated](/use/updates).

**Update channel:** `andronix` updates itself from the **stable** channel (the release) by default.

- **Beta builds:** `andronix update --channel beta --token ''` switches to beta builds of the installer. This is a Premium early-access perk. The token comes from the app: Premium › Beta installer builds › **Copy beta command** copies the whole command. The token is only valid for a limited time; if it's refused, copy the command again.
- **Back to the release:** `andronix update --channel stable`.

## Removing a distro

```bash
andronix remove <distro> [--yes] [--legacy]
```

Deletes the distro, its files and its start script. Files in `/sdcard` are not touched. It asks before deleting anything unless you pass `--yes`.

`--legacy` also deletes a copy of the same distro left by the pre-2.0 installer (for example `~/debian-fs`). The app's uninstall command includes it. See [Installs from before Andronix 2.0](/pre-2.0/older-installs).

## Removing a Modded OS edition

installer 2.0.1+

```bash
andronix remove <edition-id> [--yes] [--legacy]
```

Deletes only that exact edition, for example `andronix remove ubuntu-kde`. It never deletes the free distro or another edition in the same folder: if that edition isn't the one installed, it says what is installed, keeps it, and deletes nothing. See [Modded OS edition ids](#modded-os-edition-ids).

With a Classic edition id, `--legacy` also deletes the copy of that edition the old Andronix app (8.x and earlier) installed in Termux's home folder, if it's still there:

| Edition id | Old copy that `--legacy` deletes |
|---|---|
| `legacy-ubuntu-xfce` | `~/andronix-fs`, `~/andronix-binds`, `~/start-andronix.sh` |
| `legacy-ubuntu-kde` | `~/androkde-fs`, `~/androkde-binds`, `~/start-androkde.sh` |
| `legacy-debian` | `~/androdeb-fs`, `~/androdeb-binds`, `~/start-androdeb.sh` |
| `legacy-manjaro` | `~/androjaro-fs`, `

output.title: The Install Fails or Stops
output.text:
This page is for Andronix with **Termux**. For installs in the app, see [Linux in the app: limits and problems](/troubleshooting/in-the-app).

This page covers problems while installing a free distro, and just after. For desktop problems, see [The desktop is black, slow or closes](/termux/desktop-problems); for Termux errors, see [Termux errors](/termux/errors). If yours isn't here, see [Still stuck?](#still-stuck) at the bottom.

## The install stopped halfway

Android sometimes stops long-running apps in the background, the connection drops, or Termux gets closed by accident. None of that ruins your install.

**Fix:** paste and run the **same install command** again. The installer remembers which steps finished and picks up where it stopped. You'll see those steps marked as done or skipped.

While it installs, Andronix keeps your phone from putting Termux to sleep. If Android asks whether Termux can keep running in the background, tap **Allow**.

## Process completed (signal 9) - press Enter

This error comes from Android's **phantom process killer** (Android 12 and newer), which kills apps that start too many processes. It can hit during an install or while you use the desktop.

**Fix:** turn off the phantom process killer by following [Process completed (signal 9)](/troubleshooting/signal-9). Then run the install command again; it continues where it stopped.

Also disable battery optimization for Termux in your phone's settings.

## Not enough storage

The installer checks your free space before it starts, and warns you if it looks too low. Roughly how much a distro takes once installed:

| Install | Space used |
|---|---|
| Command line only | 250 to 400 MB |
| XFCE or LXQt desktop | 0.8 to 1.6 GB |
| MATE desktop | 1.5 to 1.9 GB |
| KDE Plasma desktop | about 2.5 GB |

Leave some extra room for the download while it unpacks. If you're short on space, free some up, pick a smaller desktop, or use the command line only. Use `andronix list` to see what's installed, and [remove](/install/uninstall) distros you don't use.

Distros can only be installed on your phone's internal storage, not on an SD card. See [Limitations](/reference/limitations#hardware-limitations).

## Download errors

- **The download failed or timed out:** check your connection and run the same command again. The download resumes instead of starting over.
- **The installer says your network hit the limit:** the fallback download source limits how many downloads come from one network. Wait a while and try again, or switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data.

## The installer warns about an old kernel

Some older phones (for example Android 8 or 9 phones on a 4.4 kernel) run a Linux kernel older than 4.8.

In the app, these desktops aren't offered on such phones: see [Requirements](/start-here/requirements#older-linux-kernels).

Desktops install and work on many of these phones, but on some the desktop stays black. The command line always works.

The app (10.0.3 and newer) shows a notice when you pick a desktop, and `andronix` warns before a desktop install, `andronix desktop` and `vncserver-start`. From installer 2.0.5 the warning reads:

```text
This phone's Linux kernel (4.4.x) is older than 4.8. Desktops work on many such phones but may stay black. If yours does: andronix desktop --legacy-drawing, or try VNC (vncserver-start). The command line always works.
```

Installer 2.0.4 still says the desktop stays black and suggests `--de none`. You can install a desktop anyway.

**If the desktop stays black:**

1. **Try legacy drawing.** In Termux, stop the desktop and open it again with `--legacy-drawing` (installer 2.0.4 or newer). Andronix remembers it for the next start.

```bash copy
   andronix desktop stop
   andronix desktop --legacy-drawing
```

2. **Try VNC.** Inside the distro, run `vncserver-start`, then connect a VNC viewer. See [Other ways to connect (VNC)](/termux/vnc).
3. **Use the command line.** Everything except the desktop works: command-line software, dev packs and servers. To skip the desktop, install with `--de none` (for example `andronix install debian --de none`) or pick **CLI Only** in the app.

**Check your kernel:** run `uname -r` in Termux. `4.4.x` or `4.9.x`? A `4.9` kernel is fine; only versions below 4.8 are affected.

**Modded OS needs kernel 4.8 or newer.** Below that, the app shows "Modded OS needs a newer kernel" and doesn't offer the editions.

Tell us how it went: [Report a problem](/troubleshooting/report-a-problem) or ask on Discord, with the output of `uname -r`.

## Your phone isn't supported by a distro

In its first step, the installer checks your phone's CPU. If a distro isn't available for it (for example, Fedora and Manjaro need a 64-bit phone), it tells you. Pick another distro from [Supported Distros](/reference/distros).

## I forgot my password

In Termux, open a root shell in the distro and set a new password for your user:

```bash copy
andronix start debian --root
passwd alex
```

Replace `debian` with your distro and `alex` with your username. To reset the desktop (VNC) password, see [Changing the desktop password](/termux/vnc#changing-the-desktop-password).

## sudo prints "unable to send audit message"

`sudo: unable to send audit message: Operation not permitted` is harmless. Your command still runs as root.

## Still stuck?

- Every install, remove, backup and restore writes a log to `~/.andronix/logs/` in Termux. Include the latest one when you ask for help.
- With installer 2.0.1 or newer, also include the output of `andronix doctor`: it shows your phone's details and the fixes Andronix applies. See [andronix doctor](/reference/andronix-command#checking-your-phone-andronix-doctor).
- [Report a problem](/troubleshooting/report-a-problem): right after a failed command, run `andronix report` in Termux (installer 2.0.2+), or use the form in the Andronix app. Either attaches your phone's details and gives you a report ID.
- Ask on our Discord, or email support@andronix.app.
- Check the [FAQ](/troubleshooting/faq).

data.delta:
In Termux, one command installs Debian with the XFCE desktop:

```bash
andronix install debian --de xfce
```

When it finishes, open the desktop full screen in Termux:X11:

```bash
andronix desktop debian
```

1. Keep Termux open while it installs.
2. If the install stops halfway, run the same install command again. It picks up where it stopped.

Sources: [The andronix command](https://docs.andronix.app/reference/andronix-command) and [Install problems](https://docs.andronix.app/termux/install-problems).
